lesson.title: Data protection impact assessments
lesson.summary: Decide when a data protection impact assessment is required, and what it must contain.

prerequisites.reason: One listed DPIA case is large-scale special-category data.
One listed DPIA case is systematic automated evaluation with significant effects.
A DPIA is a risk-based controller measure.

blocks: Where processing, especially using new technologies, is **likely to result in a high risk** to people's rights and freedoms, the controller must carry out a **data protection impact assessment** (DPIA) **before** the processing starts (Article 35(1)).
One assessment may cover a set of similar operations with similar high risks.
Article 35(3) lists cases where a DPIA is required in particular:

items: (a) systematic and extensive **evaluation** of personal aspects based on automated processing, including profiling, with decisions that have legal or similarly significant effects;
(b) **large-scale** processing of special-category data or criminal-offence data;
(c) systematic **monitoring of a publicly accessible area** on a large scale.

blocks: Each supervisory authority publishes a **list** of processing types that require a DPIA (Article 35(4)). It may also publish a list of types that do not (Article 35(5)).
Check your authority's list. It is the practical way to find cases beyond Article 35(3).
A DPIA must contain at least (Article 35(7)):

items: (a) a systematic description of the processing and its purposes;
(c) an assessment of the **risks** to people's rights and freedoms;

blocks: Seek the advice of the data protection officer, if there is one (Article 35(2)). Where appropriate, seek the views of the people affected or their representatives (Article 35(9)).
Review the DPIA at least when the risk changes (Article 35(11)).

Sunfield plans software that scores job applicants and automatically rejects low scores. That is systematic, automated evaluation with significant effects, matching Article 35(3)(a), so a DPIA is needed first.
Whether its shop cameras need one depends on scale and on the authority's list. Sunfield checks that list rather than guessing.

blocks.text: These Sunfield examples are **illustrations**. A real assessment depends on all the facts.

questions.prompt: When must a DPIA be carried out?

options.blocks: Before processing that is likely to be high risk

options.reason: A DPIA is done prior to processing.

variants.prompt: At what point does Article 35(1) require an impact assessment?

options.reason: A DPIA is done prior to processing.

options.blocks: Before processing that is likely to be high risk

questions.prompt: Which case does Article 35(3) list as requiring a DPIA?

options.reason: Not a listed case, and not normally high risk.

variants.prompt: Which processing is named in Article 35(3)?

options.reason: Not a listed case, and not normally high risk.

questions.prompt: Which element must every DPIA include?

options.blocks: An assessment of necessity and proportionality

variants.prompt: What does Article 35(7) require a DPIA to contain?

options.blocks: An assessment of necessity and proportionality

questions.prompt: Where can Sunfield find further processing types that need a DPIA?

options.blocks: Nowhere; Article 35(3) is the complete list
options.reason: Article 35(3) says "in particular". It is not exhaustive.
Article 35(4) gives the lists to supervisory authorities.
